Executive Diagnosis

Executive Summary

01
  • The site is relevant to the right search terms but almost entirely absent from page 1, 74% of tracked keywords sit in positions 51–100.
  • On-site structure (hidden navigation, thin fleet pages, no blog) is actively working against the keywords being targeted.
  • Mobile performance is poor (45/100), the channel most booking traffic will arrive through.
  • The backlink profile carries a High toxicity rating, with strong evidence of spam/negative-SEO link patterns rather than organic growth.
  • Basic on-page SEO is inconsistent across the site: widespread missing alt text, no meta descriptions on any service page checked, and duplicate/empty H1 tags.

Semrush Domain Overview

This is the baseline health check for the domain. Authority Score sits at 8, which Semrush itself flags as "Low authority", a direct reflection of the backlink and content issues covered later in this audit. Organic traffic is just 34 visits a month from 96 keywords, and that keyword count is down 31% over the tracked period. AI Search visibility (ChatGPT, Google AI Overview, Google AI Mode) is 0 across the board, only Gemini cites a single page. Traffic is also UK-concentrated: 34 visits from 73 keywords in the UK versus 0 visits from 9 keywords in the US.

Google Ads Transparency Centre, No Paid History

Searching Google's own Ads Transparency tool by domain returns zero results for ltchauffeurs.co.uk. This confirms the business has never run a Google Ads campaign on this domain. Practically, that means every visibility gap identified in this audit is the entire story, there's no paid traffic quietly compensating for the organic shortfall.

Audit Section 03

3. On-Site Structure & Content Gaps

04

Homepage Header, Navigation Fully Hidden

The homepage header shows only the logo and a hamburger menu icon, no visible text links, even on desktop. Search engines use visible top-level navigation as a signal for which pages matter most on a site; hiding it behind a menu removes that signal and adds friction for any visitor expecting a normal menu bar.

Expanded Menu, No Content Hub

Opening the hamburger menu reveals the full list: Home, Our Fleet, Our Services, About Us, Contact Us, Our Policies, My Account. There's no Blog or resources section anywhere. Without a content hub, there's no scalable way to target the long-tail, informational searches that typically build topical authority, which connects directly to the Authority Score of 8 and the 0 AI Search visibility seen in Section 1.

XL Class Fleet Page, Thin Content, Bad URL, Placeholder Price

This single page carries three separate issues. First, the URL is /product/6a8c4c8e0a43e/, a random ID instead of something readable like /fleet/xl-class-chauffeur/, losing a free keyword and click-through signal. Second, the page has no descriptive content: no capacity, no included amenities, no vehicle specs, just an image, a price, and an "Add to Cart" button, giving Google nothing to match to a search query. Third, the price shown is £0.01, a placeholder that was never replaced with real pricing, which damages trust for any real visitor who lands here.

Content Section, Unused Layout Space

This section pairs a full-height image with a short paragraph pushed into a narrow strip, leaving a large blank area with no content. This kind of unoptimized responsive layout typically hurts scannability and can affect Core Web Vitals scoring, and it's consistent with the page speed issues covered in Section 4.

Site Footer, Under-Representing the Business

The footer lists only 3 of the site's services and 4 fleet classes, with no links to a blog, locations, or additional service pages, a missed opportunity, since footers are normally a sitewide internal-linking asset. Hovering the logo also reveals a leftover link to elementpack.pro, the page-builder's own template source, which shouldn't be publicly visible on a live client site.

PageSpeed Insights, Desktop

Desktop scores 58/100 ("Needs improvement"). First Contentful Paint (1.0s) and Largest Contentful Paint (1.4s) are both reasonable, but Total Blocking Time (740ms) and Speed Index (5.9s) are flagged red, the page becomes visible quickly but stays sluggish and unresponsive while scripts finish loading.

PageSpeed Insights, Mobile

Mobile scores just 45/100 ("Poor"). Every timing metric is flagged red: First Contentful Paint 4.3s, Largest Contentful Paint 5.2s, Total Blocking Time 750ms, and a Speed Index of 13.4s, over four times slower than desktop. Since Google indexes and ranks primarily off the mobile experience, this is the version of the site that matters most for rankings, and it's currently the weakest.

5. Backlink Profile & Toxicity Risk

Backlink Audit, Overview

Semrush's Backlink Audit tool rates the profile's Overall Toxicity Score as "High," with an explicit prompt to review the most toxic links. Out of 1.7K analyzed backlinks across 745 referring domains, 558 backlinks are marked "New", meaning most of this link growth is recent, which matters for what's found in the examples below.

Toxicity Breakdown

A closer look at the toxicity bar: 110 backlinks (14.8%) are outright toxic, 21 (2.8%) are potentially toxic, and 614 (82.4%) are non-toxic. A 14.8% toxic rate is high enough to actively work against the Authority Score rather than support it.

Toxic Source Example, PBN / Guest-Post Networks

Domains like mervi.shop, ervthromycinonline.site, tokyopush188.online, and ggmap.us.com all use near-identical templated anchor text ("Trusted High DA Backlinks to Boost Domain Authority...", "Professional Guest Post Service..."). This is the signature of a private blog network or paid link-selling service, not organic mentions, toxicity scores here run 89–93.

Toxic Source Example, Gambling & Casino Link Farms

A separate cluster of sources, bestirishcasinoonline.online, onlinegamblingbonus.online, top5casino.online, casinopopular.online, are all online gambling sites with no topical connection to a chauffeur business. This pattern of unrelated, high-volume link farms pointing at one domain is a classic marker of purchased links or a negative-SEO campaign. Toxicity scores here run 93–95, the highest in the profile.

Toxic Source Example, The Fabricated URL Red Flag

The most concerning entry: a backlink from kreskogroup.com, a solar-panel blog, points to ltchauffeurs.co.uk/how-to-use-social-media-for-mlb-betting-insights/, a URL with a topic (MLB betting) that has no connection to chauffeur services and doesn't match anything else on the site. This carries the maximum toxicity score of 100 and should be treated as a priority: either the site has a hidden or compromised page, or this link was engineered purely to inflate toxic link volume.

Audit Section 06

6. Technical SEO & Crawlability

07

robots.txt

The file confirms crawling is not blocked, the highlighted Yoast "Disallow:" rule is empty, meaning it disallows nothing, and the sitemap index is correctly declared. The one oddity is that the file contains two separate "User-agent: *" blocks (a default WooCommerce block above, a Yoast block below) that were never merged into one, harmless, but a sign the file hasn't been reviewed since the site was set up.

Leftover Page-Builder Sitemap

A second, undeclared sitemap file, /bdt-template-builder-sitemap.xml, is live and publicly accessible. It was auto-generated by a page-builder plugin and lists exactly one URL: an internal utility page (?bdt-template-builder=3171) with no real content. It isn't linked from the main sitemap index, but its public existence is a third example, after the footer's elementpack.pro link and the placeholder fleet pages, of build artifacts that were never cleaned up before launch.

Audit Section 07

7. On-Page SEO Elements

08

A page-by-page check of images, meta tags, and heading structure across the homepage and three service pages surfaced the same three gaps repeating almost everywhere.

7a. Missing Alt Text

Alt text tells Google, and screen readers, what an image shows. Without it, images contribute nothing to relevance and the site is harder to use for visually impaired visitors.

Service Page, 58 of 69 Images Missing Alt Text

84% of the images on this page have no alt attribute at all. Every example shown is a Google Maps tile fetched for the booking widget's route-planning map, meaning this isn't manually-added content, it's the map widget itself generating untitled images by default.

Homepage, 60 of 83 Images Missing Alt Text

The same pattern repeats on the homepage: 60 of 83 images (72%) have no alt text, and all 83 are missing a title attribute. Again, the visible examples are the same Google Maps route-planning tiles, confirming this is a template-wide issue rather than a one-page oversight.

Wedding & Event Page, Only 1 Image Missing Alt Text

This page is the exception: only 1 of 10 images lacks alt text, and that single image is a WordPress.com analytics tracking pixel, not real content, so this page's actual images are properly tagged. It's worth noting because it proves the alt-text gap is fixable and isn't happening everywhere; it's specifically the map widget dragging the average down on other pages.

7b. Meta Titles & Meta Descriptions

Title and description tags are what show up as the clickable headline and snippet in Google's search results, missing or poorly sized tags directly hurt click-through, even on pages that do rank.

Wedding & Event Chauffeur, Title OK, Description Missing

The title tag ("Wedding & Event Chauffeur - LT Chauffeurs," 41 characters) is a good length. But the meta description is entirely missing, so Google will auto-generate a snippet from whatever text it finds on the page instead of a written, persuasive one.

Airport Transfers, Title Too Short, Description Missing

This is the more urgent of the two title issues: at 33 characters, the title is flagged as too short to make full use of the search snippet, and, like every other page checked, the description is missing entirely. Airport Transfers is likely one of the highest-intent pages on the site, which makes this gap the most costly one found in this section.

Hourly / As-Directed Service, Title OK, Description Missing

Title length is fine here too (44 characters), but the same gap appears a third time: no meta description. Three for three, every service page checked is missing this tag, which points to a sitewide habit rather than an isolated mistake.

7c. Heading Tag Structure

A page should generally carry one H1 that states its main topic, with H2–H6 nested underneath it. Multiple or empty H1 tags dilute that signal for search engines.

Wedding & Event Page, 3 H1 Tags, At Least 2 Empty

The page carries 3 separate H1 tags, and at least two of them are completely blank, no text at all, sitting alongside genuine content headings like "Route Planning" (H3) and the marketing copy under H2. Empty H1s pass zero information to Google, and having three on one page dilutes whichever one search engines decide is the "real" topic signal.

Airport Transfers, Widget Microcopy Used as Headings

The main H1 correctly reads "Airport Transfers." Further down, though, the booking widget's step numbers and labels, "1," "2," "3," "Enter Ride Details," "Choose a vehicle," "Place Order," "Route Map", are marked up as H4 and H6 tags, and a second, blank H1 also appears later on the page. Heading levels are being used to style the widget rather than to describe real content structure.

Homepage, 3 H1 Tags Again

The homepage's H2 copy reads well on its own, "An effortless departure," "Tailored to your rhythm," "Seamless Booking, Unmatched Comfort", followed by six clearly-labelled H4 feature headings. The structural problem is the same one seen on the other pages: 3 H1 tags on a single page instead of one.

Pattern: every page checked has more than one H1, and several are empty. This almost certainly comes from the page-builder plugin wrapping widgets (like the booking/route-planning tool) in its own default heading tags that were never given real text, the same unfinished-build signature already seen in Sections 3 and 6.
Priority Framework

Priority Areas

09
  • Disavow the toxic backlink set and investigate the fabricated betting-related target URL for signs of a compromised page.
  • Fix mobile performance, the 45/100 score is the experience most prospective clients actually have.
  • Rebuild fleet/product pages with real specifications, capacity, and included amenities.
  • Expose primary navigation and launch a blog to support long-tail rankings and Authority Score growth.
  • Clean up loose ends, placeholder pricing, leftover template links/sitemaps, and layout spacing.
  • Fix on-page fundamentals, add alt text to widget-generated images, write a meta description for every service page, and reduce each page to a single, meaningful H1.
Implementation Roadmap

Three-Month Action Plan

10

The priorities above, phased into a sequence: stop the damage first, fix what's stopping existing keywords from ranking second, then start building the authority needed to grow beyond them.

Month 1

Stabilize & Clean Up

Remove what's actively hurting the site and bank the fastest, lowest-effort wins.
  • Investigate the fabricated "MLB betting" URL and disavow the toxic/PBN/gambling backlink set
  • Replace the £0.01 placeholder price on the XL Class page
  • Write a meta description for every service page
  • Fix duplicate and empty H1 tags sitewide
  • Add alt text to the map widget's images (one template fix, applies across every page)
  • Remove leftover build artifacts, footer template link, rogue sitemap, and merge the duplicate robots.txt blocks
Month 2

Rebuild & Strengthen

Fix the structural and performance issues stopping already-relevant keywords from ranking.
  • Rebuild fleet pages with real specs, capacity, and amenities; move to descriptive URLs
  • Expose primary navigation as crawlable links instead of a hidden hamburger menu
  • Improve mobile page speed, targeting Total Blocking Time and Speed Index
  • Fix unused layout spacing; expand the footer with full service, fleet, and location links
  • Plan the blog/content hub structure and topics
Month 3

Build Authority & Content

Start converting existing keyword relevance into real rankings and traffic.
  • Publish the first blog content targeting long-tail keywords the site already targets but doesn't rank for
  • Begin earning legitimate backlinks to replace the disavowed links and lift the Authority Score
  • Re-run the full audit, rankings, speed, backlink profile, to measure progress against this baseline
  • Reprioritize months 4–6 based on what has actually moved
